what_this_is: The SHORT list every session reads at START — and its live contents are RENDERED INTO CLAUDE.md by scripts/ops/render_session_brief.py, because CLAUDE.md is the only channel that reliably reaches a session before its first tool call. Hooks do NOT run on Claude Code on the web (verified 2026-08-26: the SessionStart contract's output was absent from the session context; 1,379 consecutive 'Found 0 total hooks in registry' log lines on 2026-08-20), and CI guards fire at MERGE, which is far too late to make the work correct in the first place.
every_row_declares_how_it_leaves: `clears_when` names the OBSERVABLE condition that removes the row. 'the fix works' is not one; 'the mechanism is seen acting on a named trade' is. A row nobody can tell is finished never gets cleared.
loud_means_report_it_every_session: A row with `loud: true` must be REPORTED ON in the session's closing summary — checked and stated, not silently carried. Operator directive 2026-08-26: 'keep a LOUD backlog item for EVERY SESSION to check and report on it till it's implemented correctly and the mechanism has been verified.'

items.summary: The MHG disjoint-OCA over-cover was CLEARED by hand; the mechanism that should have caught and reported it is NOT yet proven.
items.detail: ib_paper MHG held a 29-lot position against TWO disjoint OCA groups — 58 lots of resting stop, 200%. OCA cancels only WITHIN a group, so one stop firing flattens the position and the other group's legs sell another 29 into a naked SHORT. The stranded leg was cancelled 2026-08-26 in a maintenance window (issues #10332-#10338) and the position now rests under ONE group (oca-protect-t4796, STP 6.364 + LMT 7.1415) matching journal trade 4796. THAT IS THE SYMPTOM CLEARED, NOT THE MECHANISM VERIFIED. Two mechanisms remain unproven on a real event: (1) _emit_stop_over_cover_alert — shipped 2026-08-25, reaches the operator feed, and has never fired on a NEW over-cover; the three ib_stop_over_cover rows in the feed predate the clear. (2) cancel-ib-order's reporting — it read the successful cancel as refused_by_venue (fixed 2026-08-26, BL-20260826-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-READS-ERROR-202-AS-A-REFUSAL), and that fix has run against a fake venue only. === 2026-08-26, session b9kyip — CRITERION (a) IS NOW SATISFIED; THE ROW STAYS OPEN because it requires BOTH. (a) MET, and verified the way the criterion demands — by FINDING THE ROW in /api/bot/logs?level=error, not by reading code. A NEW disjoint-group over-cover paged the operator feed at 2026-08-26T15:17:19Z: 'ib_paper/MGC: position 50.0 but resting STOP qty totals 101.0 (202%) across 2 DISJOINT OCA groups 834864174(clientId=597, other_session), oca-protect-t5007(clientId=497, this_session)'. A DIFFERENT symbol from the MHG event cleared by hand, so a genuinely new detection, not an echo. Population: the ERROR+ feed, limit=1000 returning 396 rows (a SHORT page, so the tail is proven), spanning 2026-08-20T10:58:50Z to 2026-08-26T15:17:19Z, containing 10 over-cover rows. (b) NOT met — cancel-ib-order has still not run against the real gateway. AND THE MGC PAGE NAMES WHY (b) IS HARD, which is the part to carry forward: one group was submitted by clientId 597 while the trader runs 497, and IB binds cancel rights to the submitter, so the trader CANNOT cancel that leg itself. Same shape as OO-20260825-IB-PAPER-MHG-STOP-OVER-COVER being 'blocked on WORK, not a decision' — a repair path that assumes the trader can cancel any leg it can SEE is not a repair path. SEPARATELY the Bybit half shipped 2026-08-26 IS ALSO FIRING: 'bybit_1/SOLUSDT: position 292.3 but resting SL legs total 2500.6 (855%)' at 09:37:59Z, the largest in the feed; reduceOnly, so NOT the naked-reverse hazard — the harm is the 20-leg cap and a dead trade's leg cutting a live position. bybit_1 is demo and ib_paper is paper, so NO REAL MONEY is exposed by either; stated so the severity is not over-read.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) a NEW disjoint-group over-cover is detected and PAGES the operator through outcomes.jsonl — verified by finding the row in /api/bot/logs?level=error, not by reading the code; and (b) cancel-ib-order is exercised against the real gateway and reports a cancel's outcome correctly. A synthetic test passing is NOT either half.

items.summary: journalTrust now flags accounts whose journal disagrees with the broker — but the ledger it reads has exactly ONE account in it.
items.detail: /api/bot/trades/closed and /api/bot/performance now carry journalTrust, resolved from comms/broker_truth_ledger.json. That ledger lists bybit_2 and nothing else, because it is populated BY HAND from an operator's venue export. So every other account grades `no_record`, which means NOBODY HAS RECONCILED IT — never that it reconciles. A session reading `no_record` as a clean bill of health has reintroduced the exact bug the field was built to fix.
items.clears_when: Either every real-money account has been reconciled against its venue at least once (so `no_record` on a real-money account becomes a genuine anomaly), or an automated reconciliation replaces the hand-populated ledger.
items.affects: Any session quoting a per-account PnL figure. Read the journalTrust state before quoting a sum; `no_record` is not evidence of agreement.
items.observed_live: 2026-08-26T10:10Z, deployed sha 510fbb6a: the flag works and its coverage limit is confirmed rather than assumed. bybit_2 reads known_divergent on 200/200 rows; bybit_1 / alpaca_paper / ib_paper all read no_record; /api/bot/performance?window=all reports accountsKnownDivergent:[bybit_2] and accountsUnrecorded:[alpaca_live]. Every account except one is therefore UNRECONCILED, which is what this row exists to keep visible — no_record is not a clean bill of health.
items.observation: || 2026-08-26 (b9kyip): re-checked on the deployed /api/bot/performance?window=all -- journalTrust reads {readState: read, accountsKnownDivergent: [bybit_2], accountsUnrecorded: [alpaca_live], accountsUnreadable: []}. items.summary: /api/diag/ib_open_orders serves a STALE, monotonically-growing order view. Do not conclude an order's absence or presence from it.
items.detail: ib_insync's openTrades() reads an ACCUMULATED cache and reqAllOpenOrders only ADDS to it, while cancel callbacks reach the SUBMITTING client only — so the read-only client the route uses never learns of a cancel it did not issue. Measured: the route and a fresh client differed by EXACTLY a cancelled pair while agreeing on all six other orders. The envelope now carries a stale_read_caveat. The ENFORCING path (the naked sweep, on the trader's own client) is unaffected.
items.clears_when: The route builds a FRESH client per read and a measurement shows it agreeing with a known-current view. Needs a real gateway to verify, so it cannot be closed from a sandbox.
items.affects: Any session reasoning about IB resting orders — including over-cover analysis, which is what it was used for on 2026-08-26.
items.observation: 2026-08-26 (b9kyip): the caveat BIT AGAIN, in the exact way the row predicts. After cancelling MGC order 422 against the real gateway the immediate verification re-read still showed the leg, contradicting the venue's own error-202 acknowledgement; two fresh-process dry runs (not_found, order count 8 -> 6) established the cancel HAD taken effect. Do not conclude an order's presence from this route -- verify against a FRESH client.

items.summary: The generated SESSION-BRIEF block in CLAUDE.md is the mechanism this session shipped in place of a cap and an adjective, and NO fresh session has ever read it. Shipped and working are different states; only a real session acting on the block settles it.

items.why_it_matters: If the block is not read, the register is exactly the thing it replaced: a file that looks like a follow-up mechanism and is not one. That failure is invisible -- an unread brief and a brief with nothing due are byte-identical from outside, which is the 'we did not look' vs 'we looked and found nothing' collapse this repo has a guard family for.

items.summary: The stray-OCA-group sweep that fixes the over-cover GENERATOR shipped at annotate and is armed on NO account. Do not arm it before reading the MES finding below -- as written it would cancel MES's only protection.
items.detail: PRs #10352 + #10353 shipped src/runtime/stray_oca_groups.py and wired it into IBClient.place_protective. It closes the generator caught in the act at 2026-08-26T02:08:35Z on ib_paper/MHG: place_protective's keyed pre-cancel is scoped BY NAME to oca-protect-t<trade_id>, so a group resting under a legacy (oca-protect-<reqId>) or bare-numeric (e.g. 834864174) name is never a cancellation candidate and the re-arm mints a SECOND, non-mutually-cancelling group beside it -- 300% across 3 groups, with no 'no oca_key' warning, no Error 10147 and no survivor-join log, i.e. none of the three signatures of the previously-known defect. LIVE STATE: PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_MODE=annotate (the shipped default -- the decision runs in full and cancels NOTHING) and PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS is UNSET, which for this knob means NONE (deliberately the opposite polarity to CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS / NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS). TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE ARMING. (1) ib_paper/MES rests a single LEGACY-named group oca-protect-408, which the sweep classifies stray_unkeyed and would CANCEL -- and it is MES's ONLY protection. Arming without resolving that trades one safety defect for a worse one. (2) annotate writes NO durable soak file (unlike PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE, which writes protection_reassert_soak.jsonl), only a trader-journal WARNING -- so 'observe first' means a journalctl pull, not a log endpoint.
items.clears_when: The sweep is armed on ib_paper AND a row is observed in which it classified a real leg and acted -- naming the trade, the stray group and the preserved group. Shipping is not the observable; a cancel that happened is. Alternatively, the row clears if the operator decides not to arm it, recorded as that decision.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: annotate and apply are byte-identical from every surface except the trader journal, so a sweep that is silently mis-scoped looks exactly like one that found nothing to do.
items.observation: CHECKED 2026-08-29 (session 01UTcLyMtHKYkhMiMKk1asbv). NOT CLEARED - still unarmed, and I did NOT arm it. TWO OBSERVATIONS, both reads. (1) THE MES BLOCKER STILL HOLDS AND IS WORSE THAN THIS ROW RECORDED. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-29T06:21:15Z returns EXACTLY 2 resting orders, both MES, both under the legacy-named group 'oca-protect-408': an LMT SELL 15 @ 8390.5 and an STP SELL 15 @ 7533.75. So the group the sweep would classify stray_unkeyed and CANCEL is not merely 'MES's only protection' (this row's wording) - it is a COMPLETE TWO-SIDED bracket, stop AND target, and it is the account's only resting protection of any kind. Arming without resolving it would remove both legs. CAVEAT, stated because the route requires it: the response carries stale_read_caveat=true (BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW), so verify against a fresh client before ACTING. Staleness here would mean the orders are already gone, i.e. it can only make me OVER-state the blocker - the conservative direction for a do-not-arm conclusion. (2) THIS ROW'S OWN PRESCRIBED OBSERVATION METHOD DOES NOT WORK AT THE AVAILABLE PAGE SIZE, which is why 'observe first' has produced nothing in 3 days. The row says annotate writes no durable soak so observing means a journalctl pull. Measured: /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service&lines=1000 returns 1000 lines spanning 06:18:00-06:21:48Z - a 3 min 48 s window, because the trader is that chatty. Grep over it: 0 sweep verdict literals (stray_unkeyed/sibling_keyed/keep_target), 0 'oca-protect' strings, and 0 protective-placement lines. The sweep only runs on place_protective's KEYED path, which did not fire once in that window - so the silence is 'the trigger did not fire', NOT 'it fired and found nothing'. Those are different states. POSITIVE CONTROL, so the zero is not read as absence: the same grep over the same 1000 lines found 4 naked/coverage-sweep ERROR rows, so the probe finds things when they are there. CONSEQUENCE: this item cannot clear via the method it names - a sparse event cannot be caught in a ~4-minute page. Clearing it needs either a durable soak file (the shape PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE already has via protection_reassert_soak.jsonl), or a journalctl pull bounded by --since rather than by line count.

items.summary: ib_paper/MGC: the exchange holds 50 and the journal declares 51, and NO IB-side detector covers that. It did not self-heal.
items.detail: After the 2026-08-26 stray-leg cancellation on ib_paper/MGC, the exchange position read short 50 while journal trade 5007 declares position_size 51 -- still divergent ~1h25m later (re-read 21:05Z), so this is not a settlement lag. CONTROL: MHG 29/29 and MES 15/15 agree exactly on the same read, so it is not a reader artefact. Protection rests at 51 against a position of 50 = 102%, which is over-covered by one lot. NOTHING DETECTS IT: the IB over-cover page requires DISJOINT OCA groups and there is only one group here, and journal_qty_divergent -- the detector that would catch exactly this -- exists only in _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions, never on the IB path. The likely origin is that a stray leg FILLED for one lot and the journal never learned (BL-20260826-A-STRAY-OCA-LEG-FILLED-AND-THE-JOURNAL-NEVER-LEARNED).
items.clears_when: Either the journal row is reconciled to the exchange quantity, or an IB-side journal_qty_divergent detector exists and reports on this position. A later read that happens to agree does NOT clear it -- the position closing would make the divergence unobservable rather than resolved.
items.affects: Any session quoting ib_paper position sizes or grading MGC protection coverage. 102% here is the journal over-declaring, not the venue over-protecting.

items.summary: The T2 research queue + dispatcher is built and green but has NEVER dispatched anything; its cron has never fired and its GPU route has never been exercised.
items.detail: PR #10365 (draft) ships research/queue/*.yaml, the R4 power gate (5 states), the routing decision (4 states), scripts/research/dispatch_queue.py and a daily cron workflow. 51 tests pass and guards are PASS 41/FAIL 0 — but EVERY dispatch so far has been a dry run or a stubbed _fire in a test. Nothing has been routed to a real runner, a real trainer job, or a real GPU burst. ⚠️ THE GPU PATH IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the operator chose 'fire everything including GPU', so the first real armed run is the first time this spends money unattended. Three gates are supposed to bound it — the burst workflow's ledger preflight against the $10/month cap, its GPU_BURST_ARMED gate, and the dispatcher's own --max-gpu-dispatches-per-run — and NONE of the three has been observed holding against this dispatcher. A test with a stubbed _fire proves the counter advances; it proves nothing about the ledger preflight. Also unproven: the last_dispatched_at stamp round-trip. It lands via the commit-to-main auto-merge PR, so a second dispatcher run inside that PR's window would RE-FIRE the same job. That race is documented in the module and has never been observed either way. ⚠️ OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-27, AFTER #10365 MERGED (28e47d97): the dispatcher stays DRY. The daily 06:20Z cron passes no --fire and MUST NOT be armed until a session has read one real dry-run report and confirmed the routing and the power gate behave on live queue contents. Arming is then a deliberate follow-up, not a default. Do not read the merge as arming it, and do not flip `fire: true` on inference from a busy research task — the operator's stated reason is that none of the three spend gates has ever been observed holding against THIS dispatcher.
items.clears_when: BOTH: (a) a queued job is dispatched for real by the dispatcher (not a dry run, not a stubbed _fire) and its rows land in the store the job declares in `lands.store`, verified by reading that store — not by the workflow exiting 0; and (b) a recurring (non-`once`) job is observed NOT re-firing on the dispatcher run immediately after its first fire, which is the stamp race actually being exercised. Until a GPU-routed job has been fired once with the ledger preflight observed refusing or admitting it, do not describe the spend gates as verified.

items.summary: Lane P (#10364, Tier-3) is green and awaiting operator approval; NOBODY has measured which compat-matrix verdicts it actually moves.
items.detail: PR #10364 changes the standard arm so it stops grading an intra-day resetting brake as a terminal account-killer, and REFUSES (verdict UNGRADED) instead of sizing off a synthetic $10,000 when the live balance cannot be established. All four checks are green as of 2026-08-27T11:02Z. ⚠️ THE CASE FOR IT IS ARGUED FROM THE MECHANISM, NOT FROM A MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER. The session that wrote it could not run the compat matrix (no numpy in the sandbox), so the number of verdicts that flip, and their direction, is UNKNOWN. That is exactly the evidence an operator approving a Tier-3 sizing/gating change should have. research/queue/RQ-20260827-001.yaml exists precisely to produce it — a deterministic re-grade routed to a runner — but it cannot run until #10365 merges and the dispatcher is armed, so the two PRs are coupled in that one direction. ⚠️ STATUS MOVED 2026-08-27: #10364 was APPROVED AND MERGED (f2ea9e44) WITHOUT the before/after diff, which the operator is entitled to do and which this row records rather than smooths over — so the pending decision is settled and what remains is purely the unmeasured verification. #10365 has since merged, so RQ-20260827-001 now EXISTS in the queue and is loadable; it has not run, because the dispatcher is deliberately left dry (see the dispatcher row). The measurement is therefore blocked on the same arming decision, and the cheap unblock is to dispatch gld-compat-matrix.yml by hand rather than to arm the dispatcher for it.
items.clears_when: The before/after verdict diff has been produced and READ — by RQ-20260827-001 running, or by dispatching the compat matrix by hand — and its direction and magnitude recorded. ⚠️ The change is ALREADY LIVE ON MAIN, so this is no longer evidence-before-approval; it is checking a merged Tier-3 sizing/gating change did what its mechanism argued. If the diff shows verdicts moving in an unexpected direction, that is a revert conversation, not a note.
items.observation:
⚠️ CORRECTED LATER THE SAME SESSION — MY EARLIER OBSERVATION ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG IN THE PERMISSIVE DIRECTION. I recorded 'EVERY MOVE IS MORE CONSERVATIVE; NOTHING moved skip->ROUTE'. That was true of the two ledgers measured and is FALSE IN GENERAL — they carried no drawdown deep enough to make the OLD static model declare a terminal breach, so only ONE of Lane P's two defects was being exercised. The drawdown half was then isolated (seed EVERY balance at 10,000 — the figure the BEFORE arm hardcodes — so the size term is numerically identical and only the drawdown code path differs; control 11/11 equal size). On a ledger carrying a sustained -20R drawdown it moves 10 of 11 accounts skip->ROUTE, with survival 0.800-0.857 -> EXACTLY 1.0 and p_breach 0.143-0.200 -> EXACTLY 0.0 on every one. breakout_1 (prop, declared ruleset) does NOT move — the control showing the change is correctly scoped to the standard arm. A stated prediction was FALSIFIED on the way and that is what exposed the mechanism: I predicted a spread-across-days drawdown would diverge and a same-day-concentrated one would not; BOTH diverged identically, so it is not a time-distribution effect — the standard arm simply cannot register a terminal breach any more. Had I run only the spread arm I would have reported a correct number under a wrong explanation. REVISED BOTTOM LINE: Lane P's two halves move verdicts in OPPOSITE directions — size resolution is MORE CONSERVATIVE (3 of 11 on a positive book, killing false ROUTEs off a synthetic $10k), the drawdown model is MORE PERMISSIVE (10 of 11 on a drawdown-heavy book). Both are defensible as corrections; neither is a regression on its own terms. But an operator approving this on my earlier sentence would have been misled. CONSEQUENCE FILED SEPARATELY: survival and p_breach are now CONSTANTS on standard accounts, so two of the gate's three criteria no longer discriminate, and BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP's blocking finding is probably unreproducible — BL-20260829-LANE-P-MAY-VOID-THE-GLD-SURVIVAL-SKIP. || 2026-08-29 (r6-vm-residency, overnight): THE DIFF IS PRODUCED AND READ. Direction question ANSWERED — NO REVERT CONVERSATION. Full working: docs/research/lane-p-compat-verdict-diff-2026-08-29.md.
WHY IT COULD RUN NOW: the 08-27 blocker was 'no numpy in the sandbox' — a missing DEPENDENCY, not a missing capability. pip install -r requirements-test.txt gives numpy 2.4.6 / pandas 3.0.5 / scipy / sklearn. The dispatcher was never needed and STAYS DRY.
METHOD: only the CODE varies — git worktree at f2ea9e44^ vs HEAD, with the ledger byte-identical (sha256 pinned), config/accounts.yaml COPIED INTO the before-tree so config drift cannot confound, one live /api/bot/accounts/balances read seeded into a local balance_snapshots table (DDL lifted VERBATIM from database.py:868, and read back through the repo's OWN Database.get_latest_balance_snapshots to confirm all 11), and --seed 20260829 --n-paths 300 throughout. Positive control first: account_rulesets.py differs between trees and standard_account_size.py is ABSENT in the before-tree, so the A/B is not measuring nothing. TWO ledgers (+213.5R and -12.2R) to bracket the outcome space.
RESULT with real balances: POSITIVE ledger 3 of 11 verdicts move — alpaca_live ROUTE->skip (synthetic $10,000 -> real $200.10), bybit_2 ROUTE->skip ($10,000 -> $305.18, and bybit_2 is MAINNET), ib_live ROUTE->UNGRADED (balance unreadable). NEGATIVE ledger 1 of 11 — ib_live skip->UNGRADED. EVERY MOVE IS MORE CONSERVATIVE; NOTHING moved skip->ROUTE, nothing became more permissive. The two ROUTE->skip moves are the defect caught in the act on REAL MONEY: the synthetic $10k made a $200 and a $305 account look routable. The seven accounts holding $66k-$1.34M were graded against a SMALLER synthetic figure and are unchanged, which is why the magnitude is modest and concentrated exactly where the mechanism predicted.
⚠️ ONLY ONE OF LANE P'S TWO DEFECTS SHOWS MOVEMENT. All of it is attributable to SIZE RESOLUTION; the drawdown-type half (static terminal floor -> intra-day resetting brake) moved NO verdict on either ledger. That is recorded as UNMEASURED, not as no-effect — these ledgers plausibly do not stress it, and a book with a deep early drawdown is the probe that would.
⚠️ WHAT REMAINS: the ledger is SYNTHETIC. This measures which verdicts Lane P MOVES (the row's question), holding the book fixed; it is NOT the true gld_pullback_1h verdict set, which still wants gld-compat-matrix.yml dispatched (its emit half needs Yahoo, firewalled in-sandbox). Balances are one point-in-time snapshot (age 2391s) and bybit_2 at $305.18 sits near enough a threshold to be hour-sensitive. KEEPING THE ROW OPEN, NARROWED: the dangerous outcome (an unexpected direction) is definitively ruled out; what is left is the real-ledger magnitude. ||

items.summary: R6 is ANSWERED and its answer is a REFUSAL: do not retire the trainer yet. One process on it genuinely requires 24/7 residency — the L2 order-flow capture, whose data is forward-only and cannot be re-derived. Where it lives if the trainer does not is an OPERATOR call, and it is the only thing between the current state and reclaiming 1 OCPU / 6 GB.
items.detail: Measured 2026-08-28/29 (diag #10391, #10392; docs/research/R6-VM-RESIDENCY-VERDICT-2026-08-28.md). `ict-orderflow-capture.service`: active 44 days, PID 728, 87.4 MB RSS, 3h53m CPU = 0.37% of one core, verified writing (newest row 2026-08-28T23:50:00Z vs same-command `date -u` 23:58:09). Its manifest: 'The capture is FORWARD-ONLY (no L2 history)'. An ephemeral 6h-ceiling runner takes an unbackfillable gap at every handoff, so this is NOT runner-portable — it needs AN always-on host, just not necessarily THIS one. WHY A FRESH SESSION NEEDS THIS BEFORE IT PLANS: the roadmap and the architecture doc both said for a day that R6 was 'unblocked' with an INFERRED answer of 'nothing still qualifies'. A session that acts on that framing retires the box and silently ends the one data stream nothing can reproduce. Both docs are now corrected, but the inference is the intuitive one and will recur. ALSO: R3 proved COMPUTE is portable, not ACQUISITION — the model R3 registered as its proof (btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1) is itself the order-flow model, trained on columns only this capture produces.
items.clears_when: The operator decides the capture's home and the decision is RECORDED — one of: (a) it is relocated to a named always-on host and observed writing there (verified by reading a fresh row's ts, not by the unit reporting active — the two came apart in the evidence above); or (b) the operator accepts losing the flow-model family and says so explicitly; or (c) the trainer is kept for this purpose as a stated decision rather than by default. Retiring the trainer WITHOUT one of these is the outcome this row exists to prevent, and 'R6 is done' does NOT clear it — R6 produced this question, it did not answer it.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: Nothing about waiting decides where the capture lives, and the disk is at 92% with nothing monitoring the capture — so the default path is that the question gets answered accidentally, by a full disk stalling the capture silently, rather than deliberately.
items.observation: 2026-08-29: R6 run and answered. No decision taken on the capture's home — that is the operator's, and this row is the thing that stops it being taken by default.

items.summary: alpaca_live go-live is blocked on exactly ONE operator decision — keep the account CASH or convert it to MARGIN. Measured 2026-08-29: capacity.multiplier = 1 (cash). Steps 1 and 2 of the go-live sequence turn out to be the same decision, and neither branch is free.
items.detail: The go-live sequence (BL-20260824-ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-SEQUENCE) pre-registered STEP 1's decision input as status_flags.capacity.multiplier. Read 2026-08-29T00:22:41Z: multiplier=1, with cash = buying_power = regt_buying_power = equity = 200.10 (all four identical, i.e. no margin line), shorting_enabled=false, status ACTIVE, mode=dry_run (confirmed on the live diag AND in config/accounts.yaml). BY THE ROW'S OWN PROCEDURE this VOIDS STEP 1 as written: at multiplier 1 the gross-exposure multiple cannot exceed 1.0, so max_gross_exposure_pct is decorative and the bound must be restated as per-trade notional. AND IT COUPLES STEP 1 TO STEP 2, which was not visible before: you cannot short in a cash account (Reg-T short selling requires margin), so STEP 2 is an ACCOUNT CONVERSION rather than a settings toggle — and that same conversion sets multiplier to 2, which makes STEP 1's exposure cap correct again with a basis already measured. CASH keeps 6 legs 100% dead and 68.8% of routed flow unexecutable, and makes T+1 settlement live-blocking (BL-20260823-ALPACA-CASH-ACCOUNT-SETTLEMENT-UNMODELLED — premise now MEASURED true). MARGIN unlocks the flow but introduces PDT (3 day trades / 5 days under $25k) against a paper book measured at 14.9% same-day round trips (BL-20260823-NO-PDT-MODELLING-ON-ALPACA). BOTH constraints are modelled nowhere in code. SEPARATE AND NOT FIXED BY EITHER BRANCH OR BY FUNDING: sizing demands up to 12.37x account notional on one trade (scale-invariant), and the 16-leg set is net-negative on paper except uso_trend_1h at n=10.
items.clears_when: The operator states cash or margin AND it is recorded on the go-live row. That single statement unblocks the restatement of STEP 1 (which instrument), STEP 2 (whether an account conversion is happening), and which of the two unmodelled constraints has to be built. NOT cleared by funding the account — funding is step 6 of 7 and this is step 0; and NOT cleared by anyone re-reading the multiplier, which is already read.
items.why_it_cannot_be_closed_by_time: Nothing about waiting picks cash or margin, and the account sits mode:dry_run refusing everything meanwhile — so there is no accruing evidence that would decide it. The lane has already stalled once in exactly this shape: STEP 1's input was readable from 2026-08-25 and nobody read it for four days.
items.observation: 2026-08-29: multiplier read and recorded; the fork is stated and nothing was changed. No funding, no mode flip, no sizing edit, no routing edit. Awaiting the operator's one decision. | 2026-08-29: the decision is unchanged and still the operator's, but the WORK BEHIND IT SHRANK. The demanded gross-exposure multiple - the quantity STEP 1's ceiling governs - has now been MEASURED rather than inferred from the mirrors, over 369 of 4178 order_packages (all gradeable), window 2026-06-16 to 2026-08-28. Median SINGLE trade demands 3.95x the whole account at risk_pct 0.05; at the mirror-derived 2.0x ceiling 307 of 369 single trades (83.2%) breach it alone; and the largest-sample leg needs >= 11.06x to trade at its median. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ITEM: STEP 1 cannot be satisfied by choosing a ceiling value at all while risk_pct is 0.05 - the ceiling is the wrong knob and the binding parameter is risk_pct (BL-20260829-ALPACA-MIRROR-DOES-NOT-MIRROR-RISK-PCT). This does NOT resolve the cash-vs-margin question this row is about, and it is not an argument for or against funding; it means that whichever branch the operator takes, a risk_pct decision sits in front of the ceiling decision. Both are Tier-3 and neither was changed. Detail: docs/research/ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-STATUS-2026-08-29.md section 7.

there_is_no_cap: Deliberately UNCAPPED (operator-directed 2026-08-26: 'we don't want to cap the number of bugs we can track, we want to ensure that they are actually being tracked, fixed, and learned from'). An earlier version capped this at 12 rows; that was a bandaid — it bounded the LIST rather than making anything get read or fixed. What bounds it instead is that a `monitoring` row must be RE-OBSERVED on a cadence: it cannot be carried by doing nothing.
monitoring_rows_are_enforced_by_observat: kind:'monitoring' rows carry `check_every_days`, `verified_at` and `observation`. A row past its cadence is DUE and is rendered into CLAUDE.md, so the next session sees it in context before acting. Clearing it for another cycle costs one honest look: record WHAT YOU OBSERVED and today's date. It cannot be cleared by asserting progress — `observation` must state a thing that was seen. This replaces `loud`, which was just another alarm to walk past.
